neighbours.label: The preposition right after a noun naming how or how much something happens, in the slot that opens an 'in which / by which' clause: 'the way in', 'the manner in', 'the method by', 'the process by', 'the speed with', 'the ease with', 'the extent to', 'the rate at'. Side trigger: '-to' in 'up-to-date'. Quiet for the same prepositions after place, time or reason nouns ('the room in which', 'the time at which', 'the reason for which'), for 'the way of', and for 'at' after rarer speed nouns ('pace at', 'velocity at').
neighbours.short: preposition after a manner/rate noun ('the way in which')
fire: The most up-to-date review on the mechanisms of SNARE-mediated membrane fusion.
She was impressed by the way in which the children solved the puzzle together.
The manner in which the letter was delivered raised a few eyebrows.
Scientists still debate the method by which the pyramids were built.
Photosynthesis is the process by which plants turn light into sugar.
Everyone was stunned by the speed with which the fire spread across the hill.
The ease with which he learned Spanish surprised his teachers.
Nobody knew the extent to which the river had flooded the lower farms.
quiet: By one estimate, this burden amounts to $80 billion per year.
She was impressed by the room in which the children solved the puzzle together.
The house in which the letter was delivered had a bright red door.
Scientists still debate the reason for which the pyramids were built.
Spring is the season in which plants turn light into the most sugar.
Everyone remembered the night on which the fire spread across the hill.
He described the way of life in the village where he learned Spanish.
Nobody knew the time at which the river had flooded the lower farms.
